facts.statement: Hollardosteus lived during the Eifelian stage.
The species was described by Lehman in 1976.
Hollardosteus marocanus is a Middle Devonian arthrodire placoderm found in Morocco.
facts.quote: Hollardosteus marocanus is a brachythoracid arthrodire placoderm from the Middle Devonian of Morocco.

facts.statement: Remains of Hollardosteus were found in Eifelian-aged strata from the Tafilat-Maider Valley.
facts.quote: Its scrappy remains were found in Eifelian-aged strata from the Tafilat-Maider Valley.

facts.statement: The lower jaw plate of Hollardosteus has a well-developed anterior tooth that resembles those of dunkleosteids.
facts.quote: The inferognathal plate has a well-developed anterior tooth (prong), very similar in form to the inferognathals of the dunkleosteids.

facts.statement: The armor of Hollardosteus features a pattern of large, crowded tubercles, unlike the smooth armor of dunkleosteids.
facts.quote: However, the dermal surface of the armor is decorated with a pattern of large, crowded tubercules totally unlike the smooth dermal surfaces of dunkleosteid armors.

facts.statement: Due to its unique features, Hollardosteus is currently classified as Arthrodira incertae sedis pending more complete specimens.
facts.quote: This mix of peculiar features leaves H. marocanus placed as "Arthrodira incertae sedis," at least until more complete specimens are found.

facts.statement: Hollardosteus belongs to the parent group Arthrodira.
Hollardosteus is classified in the class Placodermi.
